issues.description: Method mismatch: SealSaloon.checkOrderReady. The problem statement / UML declares a public method checkOrderReady() with no parameters (SealSaloon.checkOrderReady(): void). The solution implementation defines a different public signature checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and orderMeal invokes checkOrderReady(true). This divergence means the expected public API (no-arg checkOrderReady) from the exercise description does not match the solution code, which can confuse students about which signature to implement and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification. Change the solution's public method signature to public void checkOrderReady() and update the call in orderMeal to this.checkOrderReady(). If internal debug logging is desired, implement a private overloaded helper (e.g., private void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)) and have the public no-arg method delegate to it, or use a private debug flag — but keep the public API (no-arg checkOrderReady) matching the problem statement and UML.

issues.description: Concept: checking and serving ready orders in the SealSaloon class. Problem statement specifies a parameterless method named checkOrderReady() with signature "void checkOrderReady()". The solution implementation defines a method with the same base name but a different signature: "checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)". A student reading the problem will expect to implement and call a no-argument checkOrderReady(), but the provided solution uses a boolean parameter (presumably for internal logging) which changes the public API and can confuse students about the required method signature and how/when to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signatures so the conceptual operation has a single, consistent identifier. Preferred fix: add a public no-argument method "public void checkOrderReady()" that delegates to the boolean variant (e.g., call checkOrderReady(false) or checkOrderReady(true) depending on desired default logging), and keep or make the boolean version private if it's only for internal/logging use. Alternatively, if the boolean parameter is intentional, update the problem statement to require or allow "checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)" and document the parameter's purpose.
